name: New England Truck Design
old_description: Since 1977 as an employee of Wolf Coach, Kevin Lavin has designed and built many custom emergency vehicles such as ambulances, fire trucks, brush trucks and all other types of municiple vehicles. Over the years New England Truck Design has built numerous emergency vehicles with unique bodies and features regarding the customers preferences. We stock many options for emergency lighting as well. All installation and wiring can be done in-house here at the shop. We also do repairs on just about anything.
about:
New England Truck Design operates from Sterling, Massachusetts, where it was founded in 1977 by Kevin Lavin after his tenure at Wolf Coach building custom emergency vehicles. The shop remains a family-run operation focused on heavy-duty truck fabrication.

The company designs and builds custom aluminum and stainless-steel truck bodies including dump, grain/chipper, flatbed, switch‑n‑go, fire apparatus, and specialty bodies for trucks ranging from pickups to 10‑wheelers. All fabrication is done in‑house: heavy‑walled perimeter angles, I‑beam cross members on 12‑inch centers, structural channel long sills, and plate floors up to 3/8‑inch thick. They also install BOSS snowplows, Rugby truck bodies, Torwel sanders, Protech toolboxes, fenders, lighting systems from Whelen, Federal Signal, and Trucklite, and hydraulic packages from Parker, Chelsea, and Permco.

Customers span municipal fleets (ambulances, fire trucks, brush trucks), construction and hauling contractors, military programs, and commercial operators needing grain or chipper bodies. The shop stocks emergency‑lighting components and provides full wiring and installation services for each build.

Lavin’s team emphasizes longevity over weight savings, using extruded structural sills instead of formed members and a proprietary linear cam latch that removes bell‑crank linkages, allowing higher toolbox mounting. In‑house electrical work and a policy of overbuilding for the work environment are cited as core differentiators.
